paper.title: A UCB-based Tree Search Approach to Joint Verification-Correction Strategy for Large Scale Systems

unmapped: Arms are ranked by the supremum u_k of their reward distribution (the player can repeat the best observed pull), not by the mean; regret is u_* n - sum_k u_k E(n_k)
The learner knows the constant D_0 = min_k D_{0,k} lower-bounding the mass of each distribution near its supremum
settings.definition_quote: Assume that whenever a reward is collected from machine $k$, the player can remember the tricks about reproducing such a reward ... they can select the machine of the optimal reward and repeat some previous level pull to obtain the same reward. This bandit problem is defined as RBP in this paper. ... regret of a RBP as: $u_*\cdot n-u_k\sum_{k=1}^K E(n_k)$

algorithms.name: UCBRB (upper confidence bound for repeatable bandits)

conditions: each arm's distribution is lower bounded near its supremum: exists D>0 with P(X >= u - eps) > D*eps for all eps>0 (Lemma 1, Galichet et al.)
tuning: index x_k^max + 4 ln(n)/(D_0 n_k) with D_0 = min_k D_{0,k}

source.quote: For all $K > 1$, if the UCBRB rule is run on $K$ machines having arbitrary reward distributions with support in $[0, 1]$, then its expected regret after any number $n$ of plays is at most $O(ln(n))$.

results.notes: Regret is defined via suprema u_k (max-reward / repeatable-bandit objective), so quantity set to 'other'. Proof gives sum_k (u_*-u_k)(8 ln n/(D(u_*-u_k)) + 1 + pi^2/6). The theorem says 'arbitrary distributions' but the proof relies on the Lemma 1 lower-bound condition, added as condition. Proof appears informal (e.g. direction of Lemma 1 inequality).

cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic K-armed bandit, large class of reward distributions, asymptotic lower bound on total regret
